documents.title: The quiet success of the repair café
documents.text:
Every second Saturday, the community hall in Aldwick fills with the whir of sewing machines and the smell of solder. Volunteers sit at tables piled with broken toasters, torn jackets and wobbly chairs, and visitors bring items they might otherwise have thrown away. Since the Aldwick Repair Café opened three years ago, its volunteers estimate that they have mended more than 2,000 objects, preventing about nine tonnes of waste.

The idea is not new; similar events have appeared in hundreds of towns. What distinguishes Aldwick's café is the number of retired engineers and tailors it has attracted. Founder Rosa Delgado says that the project gave many of them a role they feared they had lost. "Several volunteers told me they had not felt useful since they stopped working," she says. Visitors are asked to stay and watch, so that they learn how to carry out simple repairs themselves.

Not every item can be saved. Modern electronics, with glued casings and unavailable parts, defeat even the most patient volunteers, and the café now keeps a list of products that are, in its view, designed to be discarded. Ms. Delgado hopes that such records will support campaigns for a legal "right to repair." The regional government is currently consulting on a proposal that would require manufacturers to supply spare parts for ten years, a measure the café has publicly endorsed.

documents.title: Letter regarding a late shipment
documents.text:
Dear Mr. Lopez,

I write in reference to purchase order 5521, placed on 3 May for 200 units of the Hartley adjustable stand, which you confirmed would be delivered by 24 May. As of today, 2 June, our warehouse has received only 80 units, and we have heard nothing from your sales team about the remaining 120.

The delay has serious consequences. We promised delivery to our own customers, among them the Vesper chain of stores, by the end of last week, and we have been obliged to offer them a discount of 5 percent as compensation. We are therefore asking that the remaining units be shipped by express freight, at your cost, so as to arrive no later than 6 June. If this is not possible, we would accept a partial refund covering the missing units and the costs we have incurred, which amount to 1,150 dollars.

We have worked with Lopez Components for six years and have valued the relationship. I would be grateful for a reply within two working days, so that we can decide how to proceed with our customers.

Yours sincerely,
Ingrid Haugen, Purchasing Manager

documents.title: Group chat: Marketing team
documents.text:
Helen Marsh (9:15): Quick update on the autumn campaign. The agency has sent the first version of the video, and I think it's too long. It's two minutes and the brief said ninety seconds.
Kofi Mensah (9:17): I watched it. The first twenty seconds are just a logo animation. We can cut that without losing anything.
Yuna Park (9:19): Careful. The legal team insisted that the product claims at the end remain on screen for at least ten seconds, so we can't shorten the last section.
Helen Marsh (9:21): Understood. Then let's ask the agency to trim the opening and the middle part. Kofi, can you write the feedback?
Kofi Mensah (9:22): Sure, I'll send it by noon. Should I mention the music? It's quite loud compared with the voice-over.
Yuna Park (9:24): Yes, and ask for two versions: one with the current track and one with something softer. We can test both with the focus group on Thursday.
Helen Marsh (9:26): Good plan. If the agency can return the new cut by Wednesday evening, we'll be able to use the test results before the budget meeting on Friday.

documents.title: Whitby Language Exchange
documents.text: Practice your Spanish, French or Mandarin with native speakers in a relaxed atmosphere. The Whitby Language Exchange meets every Tuesday and Thursday at the Harbour Cafe from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. Each evening begins with a short presentation on a cultural topic, followed by conversation tables organized by language and level. Membership costs 12 dollars per month, and your first visit is free. Members who volunteer to host a table receive a free drink each time. Our monthly Saturday outing, which ranges from museum tours to hiking, is open to members and a guest.

documents.title: Joining the exchange
documents.text:
Hello,

I came to my first session last Tuesday and enjoyed it very much. I have a few questions. I am an advanced speaker of French and would like to practice, but my Spanish is only at beginner level. Can I attend conversation tables in both? I would also like to bring my cousin, who is visiting from Canada, to the next hiking trip. And I wonder whether I could become a host, as I have taught French for three years.

Thanks,
Alba Mendes

documents.title: Re: Joining the exchange
documents.text:
Dear Alba,

Thank you for coming and for your message. You may join any table you like, and beginners are very welcome at the Spanish table, where we often pair them with patient speakers. Guests may join a Saturday outing if the member registers them in advance and pays a small fee for transport, usually 8 dollars. The next hike is on 16 November.

We would love you to host the French table on Thursdays; our current host is moving away at the end of the month. Hosts receive a free drink as well as free membership for any month in which they run at least six sessions. Come a few minutes early on your first evening so I can show you how it works.

Best wishes,
Tomas Lindqvist, Organizer

Registration is included in the delegate fee of 180 dollars, which also covers lunch and refreshments, and a limited number of places at the reduced rate of 90 dollars remain for trainee teachers and students on presentation of a valid card. Attendees should arrive ten minutes early for popular sessions. Slides of all sessions will be sent to registered delegates within one week.

documents.title: Question about sessions
documents.text:
Dear Organizers,

I am a language teacher at a school with many students from immigrant families, and I would like to follow the sessions most relevant to my situation. I also support a few students with dyslexia. Because I have to leave at 3 p.m. to collect my son from school, I may miss the panel. Will the discussion be recorded? Also, is it possible to swap sessions if the room is full?

Thank you,
Martina Costa

documents.title: Re: Question about sessions
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Costa,

Thank you for your message. Considering your interests, I would suggest Session A on dyslexia and Session B on multilingual learners, both in Room 102. As Room 102 holds only forty people, I recommend arriving early. Sessions are not recorded, but the panel will be broadcast live and made available online the following week. If a room is full, you may go to another session; ushers will be present to help.

We look forward to seeing you.

Best wishes,
Conference Office
